_comment: LANGUAGE-INDEPENDENT rules only. Every lexical pattern lives in a locale pack under forge/locales/ — nothing in this file may contain a word in any human language. The model never free-judges at build time; it only reads what these rules measured.
_versioning: Changing anything here changes rulesVersion and therefore every derived number. The effective version published in a skill is `rulesVersion+<localePack>@<packVersion>`, so a pack change invalidates derived numbers exactly like a change here does.

style._comment: Codepoint counts. Deliberately not characters-per-word or sentences: chat messages in many languages have neither reliably, and the bucket only needs to separate a one-line reaction from a written-out explanation.

responseGate._comment: Timing and size thresholds for what counts as a reply. The lexical half of the gate (genuineAsk, chitchatReply) lives in the locale pack.
responseGate._replyWindowNote: Beyond this gap a message is no longer a reply to the line before it, just the next thing said in that thread.
responseGate._silenceNote: Silence only counts as a decision once this much later conversation activity proves the owner had the chance to answer. Without it, the unanswered tail of any corpus would read as deliberate silence.

toneBands._comment: Derived from measured interaction volume + mutual initiation, then owner-editable. The ladder is read from these keys in order, so a deployment may add or rename bands here without a code change; `S` is reserved as the forced-conservative band for sensitive roles and unresolved recipients.
toneBands._groupOnlyNote: Someone known only from group chats cannot be measured for reciprocity, so volume alone must not promote them past this band. Being in a busy group with someone is not the same as being close to them.

verification._comment: A measured pattern is only promoted to a stable trait if it recurs enough, across enough days and scenes. Prevents 'anything a polite colleague does' from being published as personality.
verification._scopeNote: Applies to the decision layer (per ask kind, per risk class) AND to per-slice style (per scene, per tone band) via analyze.evidence_strength. Both bars must clear: minSupport alone accepts one busy afternoon of an incident, and minDistinctDays alone accepts one message a day for four days. Neither is a habit.

thresholds._comment: Every behavioral cutoff the decision layer applies, in one place. These are policy, not measurement: each turns a measured share into a published rule. They are conservative by construction — being wrong about a commitment costs more than a missed reply — and they are versioned, so tightening one is reproducible rather than a local edit.

propensity._comment: Turning a per-ask-kind reply rate into a default action. Rates are judged against the OWNER's own baseline, never absolute cutoffs: someone who answers 89% of everything and 55% of disagreements is telling you something real, which a fixed 'below 35% is quiet' rule would miss entirely.
propensity._notablyLowNote: Either test may fire, whichever is looser: at least this many points below baseline, or below this fraction of it.
propensity._alwaysDraftNote: Some ask kinds ARE the gate: being asked to decide, approve or commit is never the persona's call, however reliably the owner answers it in person. A high reply rate there says 'they engage', not 'an agent may answer for them'.

risk._comment: Per risk class: did the owner settle these themselves, or route them away? Default is restrictive, and unknown always means never_settle — absence of evidence is not permission.

autonomy._comment: Who APPEARS consistently low-stakes. Clearing every bar makes someone a candidate the forge surfaces with its numbers; it never authorizes anything. Turning one on stays an explicit owner action.

escapeHatches._comment: What makes one of the owner's real lines reusable as a shape. A long line carries situation-specific facts; a marker buried mid-sentence is not the sentence's move; multi-line text is a forwarded log.
escapeHatches._declineNote: For declines, rank by repetition AND informativeness: the most frequent decline is usually a bare 'no', which teaches nothing, while a repeated line that gives the reason shows the actual pattern. Capping the weight of repetition is what lets the informative one win.

replyWindow._comment: The inbox's staleness cutoff, derived from the owner's own answered-ask latencies rather than a fixed default. Reply latency in chat is extremely front-loaded, and the distribution differs enough between people that any hardcoded value keeps items queued long after that particular person had, in practice, already decided not to answer.
replyWindow._clampNote: Floored so a very fast replier does not get an aggressively short queue, capped so a slow one does not get an unbounded one.

freshness._comment: How stale a near-realtime store may be and still be trusted for the pre-send freshness check. Only applies to sources declaring `recentReads` (an embedding application's own database) — a source with a real live tail asks the platform directly and needs no allowance, and a source with neither degrades visibly instead.
freshness._lagNote: The bound is the HOST's collection cycle, not a guess: the reference application pulls on a fixed 2-minute fallback regardless of whether its cheap probe fired, so a lag at or under that means the last cycle completed and what we are reading is what it found. 150s adds a margin because the cycle itself takes time — pinning this to exactly 120 would flag a healthy system on every slow window. Raising it past the host's actual cycle is what makes this dangerous: the check would pass while newer messages sit uncollected, and the agent would answer a question the other person has already withdrawn.
freshness._unknownNote: A store that cannot say how far behind it is counts as stale. Treating unknown as zero is the failure this whole flag exists to prevent — it is indistinguishable from 'perfectly current' at exactly the moment it matters, right before a message goes out that cannot be recalled.

burst._comment: When several consecutive incoming messages from one person count as ONE thing to answer. Chat splits a single thought across bubbles, so judging only the last bubble reads 'sign off on the contract amount / reply today / thanks' as 'thanks' — the risk words sit in a bubble the gate never looked at, and the reply becomes auto-sendable. The failure is one-directional (toward sending), which is why folding is only ever allowed to make a verdict stricter, never looser. How often it actually bites depends on the corpus; `forge report` states what this build measured rather than assuming a rate.
burst._gapNote: Consecutive same-sender messages closer together than this are one unit. Wide enough for someone typing several lines, short enough that a new topic hours later is not glued onto the old one.
burst._maxNote: Bounds how much text one classification may cover, so a very chatty stretch cannot accumulate every risk class in the pack and make every reply draft-only for reasons nobody can trace.
burst._bubbleNote: The same idea applied to the OWNER's own side: consecutive messages closer together than this are one reply sent as several bubbles. Shorter than gapSeconds because writing a follow-up bubble takes less time than a counterparty noticing and answering. Feeds the measured messages-per-reply figure, which is what stops a skill from asserting 'always reply once' or 'always split' — both are guesses, and the real rate differs per person and per tone band.

people._comment: Publication thresholds for the people table.

scenes._comment: When a per-scene measurement may be rendered at all. Whether it is narrated as a HABIT is a separate, stricter question answered by `verification` (minSupport + minDistinctDays), not here — see _evidenceNote.
scenes._evidenceNote: A scene above minMessagesToRender but below the `verification` bars is still rendered, and marked thin. Hiding it would be its own error: a reader who cannot see that a situation exists concludes it never happens, which is the 'unmeasured is not a measured zero' failure in the other direction. But rendering it unmarked is worse — a rare situation is exactly where an unattended agent has the least evidence and the most to lose, and per-scene numbers carry no sample size on their face.

styleNarration._comment: Cutoffs for how length guidance is phrased. Below `veryShortCodepoints` the advice is 'one thought per message'; above `fullSentenceCodepoints' it is 'fuller sentences'. `meanSkewRatio` is when the mean is far enough above the median to be worth warning about, because a handful of pasted write-ups can pull a mean far above anything the person actually types.
